en: to put on the market; to release

examples.ko: 그 가수는 다음 주에 새 앨범을 발매해요.
examples.en: That singer is releasing a new album next week.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 게임을 올해 안에 발매하려고 해요.
examples.en: The company wants to release a new game within this year.
The song released last year is still popular.
Fans eagerly counted the days until it was released.
They released the limited edition first.
I hope they release the regular edition next year too.

explain: 주어는 가수·회사처럼 상품을 내놓는 쪽이에요. 앨범과 게임, 한정판처럼 가게에서 파는 물건에 어울리고, 앱은 '출시하다', 책은 '출간하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 팬이 앨범을 사는 건 '발매하다'가 아니라 '사다'예요.

phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the product is the subject.

phrases.en: The company released the game as a limited edition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한정판처럼 가게에서 파는 물건과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well with store-sold items such as limited editions.
phrases.en_equiv: to release as a limited edition

phrases.en: The company launched a new app.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 서비스처럼 새로 내놓는 것에는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural for newly launched things like apps or services.

explain_en: The subject is the one putting a product out, such as a singer or company. It suits albums, games and limited editions sold in stores; apps are 출시하다 and books 출간하다. A fan buying an album is simply 사다, not 발매하다.

examples.en: The graduation ceremony was held on a grand scale in the school auditorium.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 많은 손님 앞에서 결혼식을 성대히 올렸어요.
examples.en: The two held a grand wedding in front of many guests.
We plan to hold this year's festival in grand style too.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 팔순 잔치를 성대히 해 드렸어요.
examples.en: We threw a grand party for my grandfather's eightieth birthday.
The opening ceremony kicked off with great splendor.

examples.ko: 마을에서 새해맞이 행사를 성대히 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The village is preparing the New Year event on a grand scale.

explain: 결혼식, 잔치, 기념식, 개막식처럼 규모가 크고 화려한 행사 앞에 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '성대하게'나 '크게'라고 말하는 경우가 많고, '성대히'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: We held the birthday party grandly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '성대히'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 성대히, and sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: We held the shop's opening ceremony on a big scale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 규모가 큰 행사를 쉽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, everyday way to say an event was large in scale.

phrases.en: A grand feast was held in the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때는 '성대한' 꼴로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the 성대한 form when modifying a noun.

explain_en: It mostly goes with big, splendid events like weddings, parties and ceremonies. In daily talk people often say '성대하게' or '크게', while '성대히' appears more in news and writing.

examples.ko: 시청이 다음 달에 마라톤 대회를 주최해요.
examples.en: The city hall hosts a marathon next month.
Our school organized a speech contest.
Do you know who organized this event?

examples.ko: 회사에서 가족 초청 행사를 주최할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will host a family invitation event.

examples.ko: 행사를 주최하는 사람은 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: The person organizing an event has a lot to prepare.
I went to the festival organized by the city.

explain: 행사를 계획하고 여는 쪽을 '주최'라고 해요. 돈이나 물건으로 돕는 쪽은 '후원하다', 실제 운영을 맡는 쪽은 '주관하다'라서 서로 달라요. 집에서 파티를 열 때는 '열다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The company hosts a music festival in the fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사, 대회, 축제와 함께 쓰는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard pairing with events, contests, and festivals.

phrases.en: This contest is held, hosted by the city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 누가 여는지 밝힐 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in notices to say who is organizing the event.

phrases.en: The neighbors held a small market.
phrases.nuance_en: 열다 is easier and more natural in daily life.

explain_en: The side that plans and holds an event is the '주최'. The side that helps with money or goods is '후원하다' (sponsors), and the side that runs it in practice is '주관하다', so they differ. For a party at home, '열다' (to hold) is more natural.

dis.h: be the official organizer behind an event

p.n: 개최하다 focuses on the event being held, not on who organizes it.

en: to draw lots; to cast lots

examples.en: We draw lots to pick who gets the prize.
We drew the winners yesterday.
I'll tell you right away once they draw the numbers.

examples.ko: 추첨하는 모습을 인터넷으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch the drawing online.
We drew lots for seats and then sat down.
We'll hold the drawing for the event gifts tomorrow.

explain: '뽑다'는 아무거나 고르는 일에도 쓰지만 추첨하다는 운에 맡겨 당첨자나 순서를 정할 때 써요. 뽑힌 사람은 '당첨되다'를 써요. 이벤트·기숙사·청약처럼 결과가 운으로 정해지는 곳에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: Dorm rooms are decided by lottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운에 맡겨 순서나 결과를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when order or results are decided by chance.

phrases.en: The store is holding a prize draw event.
phrases.nuance_en: An event where prizes are given by drawing lots.

phrases.en: We draw lots and give gifts to three people.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking phrase meaning to give to those drawn.

explain_en: '뽑다' (pick) can mean choosing anything, but 추첨하다 is for leaving it to luck to decide winners or order. The person who is chosen is '당첨되다'. You hear it for events, dorm rooms, and housing lotteries where luck decides.

examples.ko: 영화제 폐막 행사가 오늘 저녁에 열려요.
examples.en: The film festival's closing event is held this evening.

examples.ko: 폐막을 하루 앞두고 관객이 더 많아졌어요.
examples.en: With one day left before the closing, the crowds got even bigger.
Singers performed at the Olympic closing ceremony.
When is the closing date of this exhibition?

examples.ko: 박람회 폐막 후에도 홈페이지는 계속 열려 있어요.
examples.en: The website stays open even after the expo closes.
The festival announced its close with a splendid fireworks show.

explain: 영화제, 전시회, 올림픽, 박람회처럼 기간이 정해진 큰 행사가 끝날 때 써요. 반대말은 '개막'이고, '폐막식', '폐막작', '폐막일'처럼 뒤에 붙여 많이 말해요. 일반적인 일이 끝날 때는 '끝'이나 '끝나다'를 써요.

phrases.en: They announce the awards at the closing ceremony.
phrases.nuance_en: The official ceremony that ends an event.

phrases.en: When is the closing day of the exhibition?

phrases.example: 영화제 폐막 행사에 사람이 많이 왔어요.
phrases.en: Many people came to the film festival closing event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나는 날에 열리는 행사를 넓게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader term for events held on the closing day.

explain_en: It is used when a big event with a set period ends, such as a film festival, exhibition, Olympics or expo. The opposite is '개막', and it often combines as '폐막식', '폐막작' and '폐막일'. For ordinary things ending, use '끝' or '끝나다'.
